title: Duplicate rewardTokens entries pay the same pre-loop snapshot k times and recapture the batch's own donations
description: `_payRewards` transfers `snapshot[i]` once per array element with no cumulative per-token cap, while `_snapshotRewards` writes the same pre-loop balance B into every duplicate slot. The mint loop meanwhile raises the live balance by the batch's own donation D, so k transfers succeed whenever k*B <= B+D.
impact: Protocol-directed incentive funds (StableYieldAccumulator nudgeSplit drip + BalancerPoolerV2 per-mint cut) leak back to the batcher that generated them. The donate-forward mechanic that docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.2 calls load-bearing is defeated: a batcher recaptures up to ~100% of their own batch's donation and can drive the next claimant's seed to zero. No user principal is at risk.
attackPath: 1. _snapshotRewards writes the same pre-loop balance B into every duplicate slot of the caller-supplied rewardTokens array.
2. The mint loop raises the live balance by the batch's own donation D (the pinned dispatcher donates on every mint).
3. _payRewards transfers snapshot[i] once per array element with no cumulative per-token cap.
4. k transfers succeed whenever k*B <= B+D, so the caller is paid k times out of a pot that was counted once.
5. Back-to-back batches nullify donate-forward permanently: prior pot 77.64 USDC, paid out 155.28, 0 left behind.
likelihood: medium — permissionless (any caller supplies the array), no privilege, no timing. Bounded by the batch's own donation size: at count=400 the mainnet shape gives k=9 and 704.53 of 776.40 USDC clawed back (≈90.7% self-recapture). Honest bound: at the CURRENTLY OBSERVED mainnet shape the duplicate path still fails closed (test_AtObservedShape_DuplicateStillFailsClosed) — it needs a large batch to bite.
assumptions: The pinned dispatcher donates a legal reward asset to the batcher on each mint. True today: DISPATCHER_INDEX=4, BalancerPoolerV2, primeToken()==USDS, forwards a USDC cut, so USDC is simultaneously a legal reward token and a per-mint donation.
externalRequirements: A batch large enough that k*B <= B+D. Corroborating incident lineage recorded at tx 0x6d71d6fd, block 25242986.
justification: C4 Medium. Assets are not at direct risk in the user-principal sense, but the function of the protocol IS impacted — the incentive-forwarding mechanism the spec calls load-bearing is defeated, and value leaks to a party that did not earn it. Three independent agents converged at Medium (pattern-matcher PATTERN-001 high-confidence, econ-scanner ECON-002 with mainnet magnitude, story-faithfulness F-20-01), and convergence is recorded as corroboration raising confidence, not as three findings. NOT escalated to High: no user principal, no theft of third-party deposits, and the currently observed mainnet shape still fails closed.
recommendation: Clamp to min(snapshot[i], balanceOf(this) - paidThisPass), or dedupe the array.

fixTrap.wrongFix: Re-reading balanceOf at payout. That is EXACTLY the §4.2 refactor the spec warns against, at BOTH the snapshot site and the payout site.
fixTrap.correctFix: Clamp to min(snapshot[i], balanceOf(this) - paidThisPass), or dedupe the array.
fixTrap.jointFixNote: The correct clamp ALSO fixes the FoT payout-vs-delivered gap (CLASS-018 / DEDUP-20-006), so the two must be evaluated jointly.

orchestratorRuling.verdict: MEDIUM CONFIRMED. The stated bound is CORRECTED.
orchestratorRuling.boundRetracted: DO NOT report 'the currently observed mainnet shape still fails closed' (test_AtObservedShape_DuplicateStillFailsClosed) as the thing keeping this off High. That bound is weak: the bite condition is k·B <= B + D, and D scales with `count`, which the ATTACKER CHOOSES (the reported bite point count=400 sits well inside the ~426-users-per-30M-gas-block ceiling measured elsewhere this run). A precondition the attacker can create for themselves does not cap severity.
orchestratorRuling.boundSubstituted: The load-bearing bound is DONATE-FORWARD DEFEAT, not third-party theft: an honest single claim already takes B by design, so the INCREMENTAL extraction is capped at D — the caller recapturing their OWN batch's donation. That is a real leak of protocol-directed incentive funds and a defeat of a spec-load-bearing mechanic (Medium), but it is not theft of anyone's principal (not High).
orchestratorRuling.why: Same label, sounder footing. If the report ships the weaker bound, the first reviewer to notice `count` is caller-supplied reads the Medium as under-argued.
